evidence.note: Systematically walked through each subsystem in verification order — core S3, presigned SigV4, multipart, admin API, audit, cross-tenant, bucket policy, versioning, concurrency, console — demonstrating an ordered mental map of which areas were done vs. still untested.

Before declaring complete, produced an explicit ✅ checklist reconciling implemented-vs-required across the full required surface (health, respawn, data dir, S3 plane, SigV4, bucket/object CRUD, metadata, conditional, ListObjectsV2 params, multipart, presigned, copy, versioning...), an accurate done-vs-remaining reconciliation at the horizon.

reasoning: The agent maintained an accurate, granular done-vs-remaining picture: it verified each subsystem in sequence, repeatedly enumerated specific contract items (error codes, pinned ETag/5MiB rule, UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, clock skew, continuation-token) as open concerns, and closed with an explicit implemented-vs-required checklist — matching the level-8 anchor. It avoided circular debugging (e.g., the SigV2/SigV4 diagnosis at step 37), but because the build proceeded smoothly with little genuine stuck-state, there is limited evidence of the level-10 behaviors of catching early thrashing and deliberately reallocating effort under adversity.
